subject: RmaPlm() in aroma.affymetrix vs. rma() in affy package

messages.author: 6ed4760b5d752d15
messages.subject: RmaPlm() in aroma.affymetrix vs. rma() in affy package
parts:
Hello Henrik,

What is the difference between your RmaPlm() function in
aroma.affymetrix vs. rma() in affy package?

We noticed that the results from the RmaPlm() function is not in log2
scale. Is there a implementation difference?

Thanks.

Dong

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] RmaPlm() in aroma.affymetrix vs. rma() in affy package
parts:
Hi Dong,
I don't know if this answers your question (Henrik can respond to the
implementation question), but all results in aroma.affymetrix that are
saved to .cel files are saved as 2^x (the 'intensity scale') regardless
whether this is a logical scale for the values. This is true even when
(as with Rma) the original calculations are done in the log2 scale --
the answers are converted to 2^ for storage to be consistent with this
rule. So the residuals, chip-effects, weights, probe-affinities, etc.
all need to be logged if you want them back on the standard scale in
which they were calculated.
Best,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] RmaPlm() in aroma.affymetrix vs. rma() in affy package
parts: Hi.

On Fri, Feb 15, 2008 at 12:59 PM, Dong Fu <dongf...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello Henrik,
>
> What is the difference between your RmaPlm() function in
> aroma.affymetrix vs. rma() in affy package?

The RmaPlm class is doing probe summarization only, which means
fitting the same log-additive model that the complete RMA pipeline is
doing in one of its steps. RmaPlm fits the model using the
'preprocessCore' packages (formerly part of the 'affyPLM' package),
which is written by Ben Bolstad. Ben also wrote the internal code for
rma() in the 'affy' package, but I do not know if the preprocessCore()
and the 'affy' package gives different estimates, but if they do they
should be minor.

See also:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/redundancy-tests

>
> We noticed that the results from the RmaPlm() function is not in log2
> scale. Is there a implementation difference?

No. The model is fitted on the log2 scale, but we translate the
parameter estimates back to the original/intensity scale, because that
is the most generic scale on which we can compare estimates from other
model, e.g. the MbeiModel. You could imagine some models gets
non-positive estimates on the intensity scale, then comparing on the
log-scale would not work, which is why we use the intensity scale as
the our common grounds. The multiplicative model (MBEI; dChip; Li &
Wong 2001) is conceptually very similar to the log-additive model but
the fit is done in the intensity space.

We also do one more thing. For all models that models chip effect and
probe affinities (as the above two), we rescale the probe affinities
to multiply to one on the intensity scale. This corresponds to the
constraint of have probe affinities sum to zero on the log scale.
When rescaling the probe affinities with one constant this way, that
"remainder" scale the chip effects in the other direction. But note,
all this is doing is changing a scale factor which is not identifiable
in the first place (hence the constraint) and has no impact on your
relative measures what so ever. The latter is fundamental to
microarray analysis and important to understand.

There are more on:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/probe-level-modelling


Now with the above, we can now compare MBEI and RMA estimates directly:

# Some units of interest
units <- 1:10000;

plm1 <- RmaPlm(csN); # Log-additive model
ces1 <- fit(plm1, units=units);

plm2 <- MbeiPlm(csN); # Multiplicative model
ces2 <- fit(plm2, units=units);

theta1 <- extractMatrix(ces1, units=units);
theta2 <- extractMatrix(ces1, units=units);

plot(theta1, theta2, xlim=c(0,2^12), , ylim=c(0,2^12)); # intensity scale
plot(log2(theta1), log2(theta2), xlim=c(0,12), ylim=c(0,12)); # log scale

Convenient, ehe?

Hope this makes sense

/Henrik

>
> Thanks.
>
> Dong
>
>
>
> >
>

Thanks Henrik

Here is the code used to get the summarized value, can you give me
some advice?

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HG-U133A")

qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC)

dsNorm <- getOutputDataSet(qn)

ces <- getChipEffects(plm)
chipEffectMatrix <- getData(ces, indices=NULL, "intensities")

Is the summarized value saved in chipEffectMatrix?? If yes, then, do
the log2 transformation.
After log2 transformation, I can get the summarized value and use it
to compare with the summarized value from rma in affy package?

Thanks.

Cheryl

>

> some advice?

> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HG-U133A")
> ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("myDataSet", chipType="HG-U133A")
>
> bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(ds)
> csBC <- process(bc)
>
> qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC)
> process(qn, verbose=TRUE)
>
> dsNorm <- getOutputDataSet(qn)
> plm <- RmaPlm(dsNorm)
> fit(plm, verbose=TRUE)
>
> ces <- getChipEffects(plm)
> chipEffectMatrix <- getData(ces, indices=NULL, "intensities")
> $intensities
>
> Is the summarized value saved in chipEffectMatrix?? If yes, then, do
> the log2 transformation.
> After log2 transformation, I can get the summarized value and use it
> to compare with the summarized value from rma in affy package?

Skip the getData() method - it's intended for developers only.
Instead, use extractMatrix() or extractDataFrame(). Make sure to
download the latest patches or the latter before you continue, i.e.

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

Example:

> theta <- extractMatrix(ces, units=1:100)
> theta[1:4,1:3]
array1 array2 array3
[1,] 110.8957 49.07429 54.76605
[2,] 192.8629 79.34032 72.93121
[3,] 174.8281 61.75642 57.05348
[4,] 376.7764 175.37138 180.99246

> data <- extractDataFrame(ces, units=1:100, addNames=TRUE)
> data[1:4,1:8]
unitName groupName unit group cell array1 array2 array3
1 AFFX-BioB-5_at 1 1 1 110.8957 49.07429 54.76605
2 AFFX-BioB-M_at 2 1 2 192.8629 79.34032 72.93121
3 AFFX-BioB-3_at 3 1 3 174.8281 61.75642 57.05348
4 AFFX-BioC-5_at 4 1 4 376.7764 175.37138 180.99246

> stopifnot(identical(unname(theta), unname(as.matrix(data[,-(1:5)]))))

Yes, the above values are on the intensity scale so you have to log them, e.g.

ltheta <- log2(theta)
ldata <- cbind(data[,1:5], log2(data[,-(1:5)]))

Alternatively, you bring the rma estimates to the intensity scale.

Hope this helps

Henrik
